objective: A developer can advance a game session by controlled elapsed time without starting browser timers, while the shipped page starts and stops one well-defined runtime and handles errors safely.

include: Separate explicit elapsed-seconds advancement from wall-clock observation, timers, browser events, rendering and persistence scheduling.
Create one runtime composition/lifecycle owner with injected clock/scheduler and explicit start, stop and disposal.
Keep existing game rule order, offline cap, settings, reset hooks and Decimal semantics; integrate existing autosave through a narrow port.
Test repeated start/stop, stale callbacks, exceptions and replay of identical input/action/time sequences.
exclude: A new simulation algorithm, worker-thread deployment, performance optimization, game balancing or changes to advancement order.
Save subsystem restructuring owned by SAV01, global-state migration owned by DEV01, or UI framework migration.
Claiming arbitrary tick-chunk equivalence for nonlinear game rules without an explicit gameplay requirement.

acceptance_criteria: SIM01-AC01: A documented advancement entry point takes explicit session/context and elapsed seconds. Its calculation path does not read Date.now, access localStorage/DOM, create timers or present dialogs. Supplying the same fixture and ordered actions/time steps produces the same meaningful game state.

SIM01-AC02: Clock conversion and online/offline budgeting have a single owner with named units. Zero/backwards time, below/at/above offline cap, disabled offline production and repeated catch-up preserve TST01 expectations; one elapsed period is never credited twice.

SIM01-AC03: Evaluating/loading game code creates no ticking or autosave intervals and attaches no unmanaged runtime listeners. The real page explicitly starts the runtime once after a validated state is ready, with timer IDs and listeners owned by that runtime.

SIM01-AC04: Start is idempotent, stop/dispose clears owned timers/listeners, and pending callbacks cannot mutate a stopped/disposed or superseded session. Tests demonstrate start twice, stop twice, restart, stale callback delivery and independent isolated contexts.

SIM01-AC05: A calculation/derived-state/render callback exception cannot leave the ticking guard stuck or continue unsafe autosaves. Cleanup happens reliably; the runtime enters an explicit stopped/error condition with a recoverable original save and clear recovery behavior. Tests exercise the exception and subsequent lifecycle operation.

SIM01-AC06: Before/after fixtures for representative progression/reset/offline paths preserve established rule ordering, Decimal values and settings for the same time/action sequence. Test adapters control clocks and scheduling; they do not replace game formulas.

SIM01-AC07: Browser startup, prestige/purchase, save/reload and controlled offline return use the new runtime and pass TST01 journeys without duplicate progression or timers. Update the existing guide with advancement/lifecycle owners and targeted checks; no unsupported latency claim is made.
constraints: Planning/documentation only; no implementation, enrollment, merge or deployment authority
Follow AGENTS.md, current-main Orcha standards and existing lifecycle/permissions/writer controls
Preserve licenses, valid saves, layer IDs, save key and Decimal semantics
Hard dependencies require verified delivered source/tests and fresh exact-file preparation
No permanent legacy runtime modes, duplicate canonical models or silent failure fallback
No paid services, runner provisioning or account/policy changes

dependencies.reason: Deterministic progression/offline tests and the F2 fix must be available before moving tick/lifecycle ownership.

decisions.question: Which bounded technical direction implements this review recommendation?
decisions.answer: Use explicit advancement plus a small runtime owner with clock/scheduler ports.
decisions.rationale: The existing callback mixes calculations and effects; separating those boundaries makes deterministic testing and lifecycle cleanup possible without a new engine.

owner_origin.request: Write milestones for the remaining work on the same branch.
owner_origin.scope: Remaining review-recommendation milestone documents on the existing PR #2 branch

standards.purpose: Fresh planning-run evidence; not a consumer pin

baseline: js/game.js defines the game loop and starts intervals during script evaluation; js/utils.js independently starts autosave and attaches input handlers. Clock, canvas refresh, derived-state updates and advancement share the same callback. TST01 owns the offline-unit defect repair and its regression baseline.
implementation_sequence: Pin TST01 behavior and inventory current tick/autosave/listener entry points, clock conversions and error paths.
Introduce the advancement boundary, then move scheduling/startup/cleanup to the single runtime owner while keeping a single active calculation path.
Exercise deterministic replay, lifecycle races and errors, run real-page journeys, and publish an unmerged implementation PR with before/after evidence.

Preserve context and keyboard access for changed recovery controls; measure only when making a performance claim.
verification_strategy.status: Planned; no application changes or implementation checks performed for this documentation request

risks: Moving tick order can change balances or resets; compare identical ordered input sequences rather than only final point totals.
Old queued callbacks can mutate a replacement session; bind each callback to its owning live generation/context.
Catching an error and silently continuing can persist corruption; define and verify stop/recovery semantics.
